title: Scaled-Cayley recurrent Mirror Views
hypothesis: One shared orthogonal recurrent base plus low-rank skew-symmetric per-task Cayley codes can reproduce stable task-specific recurrent dynamics with lower serialized bytes than independent dense transitions; matrix reconstruction overhead and spectral stability will set the practical frontier.
physical_object: one shared FP32 orthogonal recurrent transition Q0
mirror_coordinate: per-task low-rank skew matrices S=UVᵀ−VUᵀ, scaled through the Cayley transform, plus shared contraction scale
logical_multiplicity: 8 stable task-specific recurrent transitions over one physical base transition
controls: native per-task low-rank Cayley parameterization with identical code
spectral radius and sequence-state norm audit

development.selection_metric: trajectory NRMSE, actual serialized transition bytes, spectral radius, and solve amortization over sequence length

success_gate: Across all audit seeds, trajectory NRMSE <=1e-5, spectral radius <1, shared payload <=40% independent, and Cayley reconstruction overhead <=25% of 128-step recurrent matvec work. Native exact alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific attribution.
failure_gate: Any audit seed exceeds quality/stability/byte/compute gates; exact native Cayley alias rejects Mirror-specific value regardless of generic recurrent sharing feasibility.
boundaries: Synthetic driven linear recurrence only; no trained RNN/SSM task, sequence prediction metric, or GPU runtime claim.
Targets are generated from low-rank Cayley codes by construction; no learning/capacity result.
Cayley transition is reconstructed on switch and amortized over the frozen sequence length; report solve overhead explicitly.
